# package webhook

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/notification/webhook"
```

Package webhook is the webhook binding of OpenADR 3 notifications, for both sides: Sender delivers a VTN's notifications to the callback URLs of its subscriptions, and Handler receives them in a client.

## Types

### type Handler

```go
type Handler struct {
	// BearerToken is the token given in the subscription
	// (ObjectOperation.BearerToken). Requests without it are refused. When
	// empty, anyone who can reach the handler can send it notifications.
	BearerToken string
	// Notify is called for each notification. Required.
	Notify func(ctx context.Context, n openadr.Notification) error
	// MaxBodyBytes limits the size of a notification; 1 MiB when zero.
	MaxBodyBytes int64
	// Version is the revision of OpenADR the VTN notifies in:
	// openadr.Version310 when empty, or openadr.Version301.
	Version openadr.Version
}
```

Handler receives the notifications of a VTN: it is what a subscription's callback URL points at.

It answers the VTN's verification request (GET with an echo parameter), and for every notification (POST) checks the bearer token, decodes the body and calls Notify. The VTN is told 200 when Notify returns nil, and 500 otherwise, on which it sends the notification again later.

Notify may be called concurrently, and with the same notification more than once: delivery is at least once. Notifications tell that something changed; a client that must not miss anything still polls from time to time.

```go

```

ServeHTTP implements http.Handler.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnDelivered is called when a webhook has confirmed a notification:
	// after how many attempts, and how long after the first began.
	OnDelivered(attempts int, duration time.Duration)
	// OnFailed is called when a notification is given up on: its attempts
	// are used up, the webhook refused it for good, or the Sender was
	// closed while it waited.
	OnFailed(attempts int, duration time.Duration, err error)
	// OnDropped is called when a notification is not even queued: the
	// queue of its webhook is full.
	OnDropped()
}
```

Metrics receives a callback for what becomes of each notification given to a Sender: exactly one of the three. The callbacks run on the Sender's goroutines, or for OnDropped on the caller's, and must not block. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

### type RefusedError

```go
type RefusedError struct{ Err error }
```

RefusedError is what SendConfirmed reports for a notification that another attempt cannot deliver: the webhook answered that it will not take it, or its URL is one the Sender does not send to.

#### func (RefusedError) Error

```go
func (e *RefusedError) Error() string
```

#### func (RefusedError) Permanent

```go
func (e *RefusedError) Permanent() bool
```

Permanent reports that trying again is of no use. A VTN that keeps notifications until they are delivered asks an error this way, so that it need not know this package.

### type Sender

```go
type Sender struct {

	// stop ends the waits between attempts when Close runs out of time;
	// stopped is cancelled with it, and ends the requests on their way.

}
```

Sender delivers notifications to webhooks. Notifications for one callback URL are delivered in the order they were sent, one at a time; a webhook that is slow or down delays those that share its worker, and nothing else.

Delivery is at least once while the Sender runs: a notification is sent again when the webhook did not confirm it, so a webhook may see one twice. It is not durable: what is queued when the process stops is lost, and so is a notification whose attempts are used up.

A Sender is safe for concurrent use. Close it to stop its workers.

#### func NewSender

```go
func NewSender(cfg SenderConfig) *Sender
```

NewSender returns a running Sender.

#### func (Sender) Close

```go
func (s *Sender) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close stops accepting notifications and waits until those that are queued have been delivered or given up on, or until ctx ends, whichever is first. When ctx ends first, the requests on their way are cancelled and what is still queued is given up on without being sent.

#### func (Sender) Send

```go
func (s *Sender) Send(callbackURL, bearerToken string, body []byte)
```

Send queues a notification for a webhook and returns at once. bearerToken is sent as the Authorization of the request when not empty.

#### func (Sender) SendConfirmed

```go
func (s *Sender) SendConfirmed(callbackURL, bearerToken string, body []byte, done func(error))
```

SendConfirmed is Send for a caller that wants to know what became of the notification. done is called exactly once, from another goroutine or, when the notification is not even queued, from this one: with nil when the webhook confirmed it, with a \*RefusedError when it will never take it, and otherwise with the reason it was given up on for now: its attempts are used up, the queue was full, the Sender was closed. A VTN uses it to keep a notification until it is delivered.

#### func (Sender) Verify

```go
func (s *Sender) Verify(ctx context.Context, callbackURL string) error
```

Verify checks that a callback URL may be used and that whoever answers there expects notifications, as OpenADR requires before a subscription is accepted: the VTN sends GET \<url>?echo=\<random> and the webhook has to answer 200 with that value as the body.

The error says what is wrong with the URL, in words fit for the client that named it.

### type SenderConfig

```go
type SenderConfig struct {
	// HTTPClient makes the requests. When nil, a client is used that does
	// not follow redirects and connects to public addresses only. A client
	// given here is used as it is: its redirect and dial rules are its own.
	HTTPClient *http.Client
	// AllowInsecure accepts callback URLs with the http scheme, and lets the
	// default client connect to loopback and private addresses. For tests
	// and closed networks; OpenADR requires https.
	AllowInsecure bool
	// Timeout bounds one request; 10 seconds when zero.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// Attempts is how often a notification is sent at most; 4 when zero.
	Attempts int
	// Backoff is the wait before the second attempt, doubled for each one
	// after, up to MaxBackoff; 1 second when zero.
	Backoff time.Duration
	// MaxBackoff is the longest wait between two attempts; 1 minute when
	// zero.
	MaxBackoff time.Duration
	// Queue is the number of notifications that may wait per worker; 256
	// when zero. A notification for a full queue is dropped.
	Queue int
	// Workers is the number of deliveries that run at once; 4 when zero.
	Workers int
	// Logger receives failed and dropped deliveries. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Metrics receives a callback for every notification; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
}
```

SenderConfig configures a Sender. The zero value is a Sender for production use: https only, public addresses only.
